claimed.text: Grusch testified that he was informed of a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme, was denied the read-ons he requested, reported this to his superiors and several inspectors general, and suffered retaliation for doing so.

Asked by Garcia whether the government possesses UAP, Grusch answered yes, on the basis of interviewing over 40 witnesses over four years, and testified that he had the people with firsthand knowledge file their own protected disclosures with the Inspector General. His account is second-hand: it rests on what those witnesses told him.
Asked by Mace, Grusch testified that biologics came with some recoveries and were nonhuman, and attributed that assessment to people with direct knowledge on the programme whom he had talked to.

Asked by Burchett, Grusch testified that he had personal knowledge of people harmed in efforts to conceal the technology; on murder he said he had to be careful and had directed people with that knowledge to the appropriate authorities.

Grusch testified that he knew the names of the special access programmes and the locations involved but could not discuss them publicly, and that he had given that information to the Inspector General and the intelligence committees. He offered Mace a cooperative and hostile witness list after the hearing.

Answering Moskowitz, Grusch testified that such programmes are paid for by misappropriation of funds and self-funding, through contractor internal research and development money, and said he was not aware of any requirement for contractors to report UAP sightings.

Grusch told Luna he had a classified conversation with Sean Kirkpatrick in April 2022, before Kirkpatrick took over AARO, and testified that Kirkpatrick's earlier statement to Congress that there was no credible evidence of extraterrestrial activity was not accurate.

Fravor's written statement describes a small white Tic Tac shaped object with no rotors or visible flight control surfaces, and says the incident was never investigated, none of his crew were questioned and tapes were never taken. Under oath he gave the chain by which the case reached investigators: Jay Stratton contacted him in 2009, and later he spoke briefly with Elizondo.

Graves's written testimony describes pilots in warning area W-72 seeing a dark gray cube inside a clear sphere and two jets taking evasive action, a squadron safety report that drew no official acknowledgement, and Americans for Safe Aerospace working with more than 30 UAP witnesses.

Gaetz described a protected disclosure from Eglin Air Force Base: on a visit he was at first refused images, radar and full crew access, then saw an image and met one crew member, and he said he alone in Congress had observed a radar sequence of four craft in a diamond formation. He added that test pilots told him the best thing for a career after a UAP experience was to forget it.

contested.text: The Department's standing response, issued in Susan Gough's name in June 2023, is that AARO had not discovered any verifiable information to substantiate claims of programmes possessing or reverse-engineering extraterrestrial materials. The board notes that it states what one office has discovered, not what exists.

After the hearing Gough stated that the Department had no information that anyone had been harmed or killed as a result of providing information to AARO. The board records that Grusch's sworn claim concerned harm in the concealment effort, so the denial answers a different question.
AARO documented at least eight approaches to Grusch between June 2023 and January 2024 and concluded that he had no intention of providing information.

At the November 2024 hearing Grothman said that no agency had been able to substantiate Grusch's claims despite members questioning them inside and outside the SCIF. On the board's reading that is in tension with Luna's 2025 statement that Oversight members could not be read in on the relevant programmes at all.

Pressed by Biggs on the 1997 Phoenix Lights, Grusch said he knew only what was in the public vernacular and that it was outside the scope of his duties; Fravor offered Biggs a lead only in a closed environment.

lead.text: On 26 July 2023 a House Oversight subcommittee took sworn testimony from Ryan Graves, retired Commander David Fravor and David Grusch, a former National Reconnaissance Office representative to the UAP task force. Grusch testified that he had been informed, in the course of his official duties, of a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme to which he was denied access.

questions: Who denied the members a SCIF before the hearing, and under what authority?
Did the cooperative and hostile witness list Grusch offered Mace ever reach the committee, and where is it now?
How many of the roughly 40 witnesses Grusch interviewed filed their own protected disclosures, and did the Inspector General adjudicate any of them?
Was the Eglin radar sequence or the crew's image ever produced to the committee?
How does AARO's later finding that none of its interviewees had firsthand knowledge square with Grusch's account of witnesses with firsthand knowledge?
How does Fravor's sworn statement that tapes were never taken fit the accounts of USS Princeton crew that recording media were removed?
Why did no subpoena follow from a hearing at which members repeatedly asked for one?

record.text: The printed record, CHRG-118hhrg53022, lists the witnesses as Ryan Graves, Executive Director of Americans for Safe Aerospace; David Grusch, former NRO representative to the task force; and Commander David Fravor (Ret.), former commanding officer, US Navy. The record shows all three were sworn.

Chairman Grothman waived six non-members onto the subcommittee for the hearing: Burchett, Luna, Gaetz, Burlison, Ocasio-Cortez and Ogles. He opened by saying that the lack of transparency on UAP had "fueled wild speculation and debate for decades".

Burchett stated on the record that members had been denied a classified briefing in a SCIF before the hearing because of the hoops involved in granting Grusch temporary clearance, and repeated after asking Grusch about murder that the SCIF had been denied.

The House Committee Repository file for the event holds the notice, roster, attendance sheet, each witness's written statement and bio, the official transcript posted 8 September 2023, and materials Burchett and Luna submitted, among them a Defense Intelligence Reference Document on vacuum-engineering propulsion, Jeremy Corbell's report The UAP Puzzle and a statement for the record by George Knapp.
Grusch's public statements had been cleared by DoD Prepublication and Security Review on 4 and 6 April 2023, a fact Luna's questioning placed on the record.
Gaetz recommended that the Eglin radar images and the flight crew's image be provided to the committee, subpoenaed if necessary; no production of that material has been recorded.

Ogles closed the member rounds by urging the chairman to demand that Grusch speak to members in a SCIF, and said that if access was denied he would volunteer to initiate the Holman Rule against any personnel, programme or agency that denied it.
Moskowitz read Chuck Schumer's disclosure language into the House record and asked Grusch whether US corporations were overcharging the government and the extra money going to programmes.

Frost used his round on the scientific and stigma side, asking Graves how Congress could connect scientists with the government's UAP work; Biggs questioned all three witnesses on misdirection, the 1997 Phoenix Lights and the 2019 classification guidelines.

The Oversight Committee is not a defense committee and has no entitlement under 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) to waived special access programme material, which the board records as a structural reason the hearing could establish allegation but not access.
On 11 January 2024 Garcia introduced H.R. 6967, the Safe Airspace for Americans Act, co-led with Grothman, to create a civilian reporting channel from the FAA to AARO.

summary.text: The hearing was held before the Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs of the Committee on Oversight and Accountability, chaired by Glenn Grothman with Robert Garcia as ranking member, and printed as Serial No. 118-53.
Tim Burchett and Anna Paulina Luna drove the hearing into existence: Garcia and Moskowitz credited Burchett's leadership from the dais, and Moskowitz thanked Burchett and Luna for pushing it forward.
The panel paired two aviator witnesses with a whistleblower alleging a concealed retrieval programme, so that the hearing record carries both the observational accounts and the programme allegations.

Grusch declined to name individuals or facilities in open session, offering the specifics only in a SCIF, and the board infers that no subpoena, compelled document production or contractor witness followed from this or the two later House hearings.
